prompt:
You are reviewing code, not writing it. Do not edit any file.

Review `check_role` (and the private helpers and constants next to it) in `src/coresight/verify.py`, and the way `verify` and `check_finding` call it, for correctness. Another Muse Code session wrote them against the tests in `tests/test_verify_role.py`, and all tests pass, as do `tests/test_verify.py` and `tests/test_verify_milestones.py`. Your job is to find what the tests do not catch.

Context:
- CoreSight turns photos of drill core trays into a geotechnical log reviewed by a geologist. When a box is approved, agents (LLMs) write a hole finding and drafts for areas of the mine (lab, safety, plant, finance). Nothing is sent without a person's approval. `check_role` is the deterministic check that a draft's words never tell the operation to stop: stopping a rig is a decision for people in charge. A failed check's detail goes back to the model as feedback, at most three attempts, then a person decides.
- Real texts it must refuse came from Muse Spark: "Do not continue drilling until the safety team reviews.", "Before the next run: stop and get geotech review. Do not drill ahead without clearance."
- Read in this order: the docstring of `tests/test_verify_role.py` (the rules), `src/coresight/verify.py`, then the tests. In `src/coresight/schemas.py`, `Draft` and `HoleFinding`.

Look for:
1. Text a safety agent could plausibly write that tells the operation to stop and still passes (other wordings, punctuation, line breaks, quotes, capitals, a title without a full stop joined to the body).
2. Text that only describes the rock or proposes a check, a review or a warning and still fails (false refusals cost a retry and a minute of the user's time).
3. The joining of title, body and action_reason in `verify` and `check_finding`: can a match cross from one field into the next, or a command at the start of the body be missed?
4. A detail that quotes the wrong words or would mislead the model that reads it.
5. Anything that raises where it should not, or is slow on a long text.

For each finding give: the function and line, a concrete input, what the code returns, what it should return and why (cite the rule in the docstring). Say how sure you are. If something is a design choice the docstring states, it is not a bug.

Rules:
- Read only. Do not edit, create or delete any file. Do not run git.
- Do not read or print `.env` or anything under `data/cache` or `data/reviews`. Do not make network calls.
- If you cannot run Python, reason from the code and say so.

Reply with: a one-line verdict (no real errors / real errors found), then the findings, most severe first.

real errors found — reasoned from the code only, did not run Python.

1. Missed stop command at start of `body` / `action_reason` when prior field has no full stop
   - Where: [verify.py](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\verify.py:199) and [verify.py](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\verify.py:321), via [_role_sentence_ids](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\verify.py:460) + [_role_is_command](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\verify.py:474).
   - Input: `Draft(title="Ground alert", body="Stop and get geotech review.")`. Joined text is `"Ground alert Stop and get geotech review."`.
   - Returns: `role ok=True`. `Stop` is mid-sentence, not after `:`/`;`, no operation word within 4, so no rule 1 match.
   - Should return: `ok=False`. Rule 1: stop verb “used as a command (at the start of the text or of a sentence…) as in ‘Stop and get geotech review’”. Body start is a sentence start; `check_role("Stop and get geotech review.")` alone fails. Same for `HoleFinding` with `body="No trend"` + `action_reason="Stop and get geotech review."`.
   - Confidence: high.

2. Rule 4 checks only the first `until` per operation
   - Where: [check_role](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\verify.py:589) loop, `break` at line 612.
   - Input: `check_role("Drill until a b c d e f g, and until lab approves.")`.
   - Returns: `ok=True`. First `until` finds `approves` 10 words later (>6), then breaks, never tries second `until`.
   - Should return: `ok=False`. Rule 4: “an operation word, then later in the same sentence ‘until’, then within six words a clearance word”. `Drill … until lab approves` with 1 word between qualifies.
   - Confidence: high.

3. `.!?` + newline/tab does not end a sentence
   - Where: [_role_sentence_ids](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\verify.py:460), line 463 checks only `text[i+1] == " "`.
   - Input A (miss): `check_role("RQD is poor.\nStop and await review.")` returns `ok=True`, should fail — `Stop` is at sentence start, rule 1 command.
   - Input B (false refusal): `check_role("Log the drill core.\nUntil the lab approves the assay, store samples.")` returns `ok=False` quoting across the newline, should pass — rule 4 requires “in the same sentence”.
   - Why: docstring says sentences end at `.!?` “followed by a space or the end”; real drafts have line breaks, and `_role_is_command` already skips `\t\n\r`.
   - Confidence: medium-high.

4. Cross-field rule 4 match with misleading quote
   - Where: [verify.py](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\verify.py:199).
   - Input: `Draft(title="The drill core is poor", body="Keep samples until lab approves the assay.")`.
   - Returns: `role ok=False` quoting `"drill core is poor Keep samples until lab approves"`.
   - Should return: `ok=True`. Title only describes rock; body has no operation word and only holds samples. Joining with `" "` with no sentence break makes them one sentence so title’s `drill` + body’s `until…approves` triggers rule 4. Detail violates “one sentence…quotes the words that matched (first match)” and misleads the model with unrelated words.
   - Confidence: high on mechanism, medium-high it should pass.

5. Cross-sentence rule 3/1 match quotes through a full stop
   - Where: [check_role](D:\Repos\coresight\src\coresight\verify.py:582) (no sentence check for rules 1–3).
   - Input: `check_role("Do not mix samples. Drilling continues as usual.")`.
   - Returns: `ok=False` quoting `"Do not mix samples. Drilling"`.
   - Should return: `ok=True`. Each sentence passes alone per docstring (“Do not mix the samples…” passes; “Continue logging…” passes / rock description passes). Quote contains a period, breaking “detail is one sentence” and suggesting a `do-not-drilling` order that does not exist. Same via `verify` with `title="Do not mix samples."`, `body="Drilling continues as usual."`.
   - Confidence: medium (rules 1–3 don’t state same-sentence, but period-in-quote + intent make this a bug, at minimum a detail bug).
